text: `&&` and `||` evaluate their right operand only when the left has not already decided the answer. This behaviour is called ___ evaluation.
explanation: It is what makes `x != null && x.length() > 0` safe, and Chapter 25 shows it is the same mechanism that makes recursion possible: a conditional must not evaluate both branches, or a recursive base case would recurse anyway. That is why `if` cannot be an ordinary method in a language with call-by-value, and why Java needs it as a construct rather than a library function.
